newsitem.title: SPAIN: FOCUS - Spanish government agrees Repsol sale.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Spanish government agrees Repsol sale.

text.p: Spain said on Friday it had approved the sale next month of the state's remaining 10 percent stake in bluechip energy group Repsol.
"By April 29 Repsol will be completely privatised," government spokesman Miguel Angel Rodriguez told reporters after the regular cabinet meeting.
He said the governemnt expected net income from the sale of around 150 billion pesetas ($1 billion).

State holding company SEPI, which manages the Repsol stake, said later the offer would initially be 22.95 million shares, of which 11.7 would be sold to small shareholders, and 2.1 million would be placed with Spanish financial institutions. Foreign institutions will be offered 9.2 million shares.
The total initial offer may be increased to 25.5 million shares. There are a further 4.5 million shares reserved for Repsol employees, adding up to the state's 30 million share stake.
Analysts said the oil firm sale should do well following the resounding success in February of the state's disposal of its last 20.9 percent stake in telecommunications firm Telefonica.
That bumper offer of at least 171 million shares was nine times oversubscribed by small investors.

Repsol's privatisation history, its reputation of being a quality company and the fact that fewer shares are on offer than with Telefonica, are seen by analysts as solid reasons for the shares to be snapped up.

"Repsol privatisations have always gone well, and in terms of quality it has a good image with the public. The fact that the (share) offer is many times smaller than for Telefonica also removes uncertainties," said Javier Borrachero, analyst at Central Hispano Bolsa in Madrid.
The state's holding in Repsol, mainly involved in the exploration, production, refining and marketing of crude oil, was worth about 177 billion pesetas at Friday's closing price of 5,910 pesetas.
Another analyst forecast the stock could subsequently soar to 7,200 pesetas on a 12-month time horizon.
"I'm very keen on Repsol. It's very undervalued compared to its European counterparts and after the adjustment in the price after the placement I see it outperforming," he said.
BCH's Borrachero saw the stock at 6,300 pesetas by year-end.
Analysts were predicting that the new shares coming to the market should be sold at a price of around 6,000 pesetas, but one analyst said anything above that price could deter investors.
"Above 6,000 pesetas would scare me a little, as with a large retail tranche the price is very important," he said. ($ = 145 Spanish Pesetas)
